'''Iyo Shrine''' (伊予神社, Iyo Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|qid=Q123376|lt=Ehime Prefecture}}. It is recorded in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' under the {{ill|Iyo Province|cs|Provincie Ijo|de|Provinz Iyo|es|Provincia de Iyo|fa|ولایت ایو|fi|Iyon provinssi|fr|Province d'Iyo|gl|Provincia de Iyo|id|Provinsi Iyo|it|Iyo (provincia)|ja|伊予国|ko|이요국|lt|Ijo žemė|min|Provinsi Iyo|nl|Iyo (provincie)|pt|Província de Iyo|ru|Иё (провинция)|sh|Iyo (provincija)|simple|Iyo Province|sk|Ijo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ијо|tr|Iyo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ійо|zh|伊予國|zh_min_nan|Iyo-kok|qid=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province}} {{ill|Iyo District, Ehime|en|Iyo District, Ehime|qid=Q1206427|lt=Iyo District, Iyo Province}} as a ''Meishin-Taisha'' (名神大社). Currently, there are two shrines claiming the title "Iyo Shrine": one in {{ill|Masaki, Ehime|en|Masaki, Ehime|qid=Q1350953|lt=Matsumae, Ehime}} and the other in {{ill|Iyo, Ehime|en|Iyo, Ehime|qid=Q838678|lt=Iyo, Ehime}}. Both are considered candidates for the historical ''Shikinaisha'' designation.<ref>Another candidate is the {{ill|Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja|伊豫豆比古命神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11380620}} in Matsuyama, but it is more commonly associated with a different ''Shikinaisha'' designation as a minor shrine.</ref>

== type ==
* Tenpyō-Shōhō 2 (766): Junior Fifth Rank, granted two servants (possibly referring to Iyozuhikonomikoto Shrine).<ref>There is also speculation that this refers to Iyozuhikonomikoto Shrine.</ref>
* Jōgan 4 (862): Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade.
* Jōgan 8 (866): Promoted to Senior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade.
* Jōgan 12 (870): Promoted to Senior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade.

=== Enshrined Deities ===
; Main deity
: {{ill|Hiko-Sashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島命}} (日子寤間命, third prince of {{ill|Emperor Kōrei|en|Emperor Kōrei|qid=Q313041|lt=Emperor Kōrei}})
; Associated Deities
: {{ill|Ehimeno Mikoto|ja|愛比売命}}  
: {{ill|Iyozuhiko no Mikoto|ja|伊予津彦命|qid=Q140446121}}  
: {{ill|Iyozuhime no Mikoto|ja|伊予津姫命|qid=Q140446123}}  
: {{ill|Emperor Kōrei|en|Emperor Kōrei|qid=Q313041|lt=Emperor Kōrei}} (大日本根子彦太瓊命)  
: {{ill|Kuwashi-hime|en|Kuwashi-hime|qid=Q11605816|lt=Hosohime no Mikoto}} (孝霊天皇's consort)  
: Hayanochiagari no Mikoto (速後上命, descendant of {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|en|Kamuyaimimi|qid=Q11588756|lt=Kami-Yaibimi no Mikoto}}, first governor of Iyo Province)  

According to the ''{{ill|Yoshōki|ja|予章記|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11371102}}'' by the {{ill|Kōno clan|ja|河野氏}}, Hiko-Sashima no Mikoto was dispatched to Iyo Province by Emperor Kōrei to suppress dissent and later enshrined in Kanzaki Manor, which became known as the Imperial Prince Palace.

=== History ===
Shrine tradition states that during the Bunji era, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|en|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|qid=Q310445|lt=Minamoto no Yoshitsune}} venerated the shrine, contributing funds for its construction, though it was later destroyed in the Bun'ei era. During the medieval period, the shrine was revered by the Kōno clan, who claimed descent from Hiko-Sashima no Mikoto. It was rebuilt by {{ill|Kawano Michinobu|ja|河野通信|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11554270}} during the Tenshō era. In the Kanbun era, the shrine began to be referred to as Shinōkyū Daimyōjin (Imperial Prince Palace Daimyōjin).

In Meiji 30 (1897), excavation at the site revealed artifacts such as Sutra containers, leading to a request for promotion to a National Shrine Rank. However, the shrine ultimately remained a Prefectural Shrine due to its limited parishioners.<ref>''Nihon no Kamigami (2) Sanyō Shikoku'', p. 320</ref>

=== Features ===
; Worship Hall  
; Main Hall  
: Nagare-zukuri style, with a copper roof.  
; Yamano Shrine  
: Enshrines {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}} and {{ill|Waraji Shrine|ja|和霊神|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579310}}.  
; Sarutahiko Shrine  
: Enshrines {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|猿田彦命|lt=Sarutahiko}}.  
; Itsukushima Shrine  
: Enshrines {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島姫命}} and five other deities.  
; Kamado Shrine  
: Enshrines Okitsuhiko no Mikoto and one other deity.  
; "Forbidden Forest"  
: A grove within the shrine grounds containing three five-tiered stone pagodas. Excavations in Meiji 30 (1897) unearthed Song dynasty porcelain jars and six bronze Sutra containers.

=== Cultural Properties ===
; Designated by Matsumae Town  
: Five-tiered pagodas.  
: Artifacts from the Sutra mound (two porcelain jars, six bronze Sutra containers).  
Both were designated cultural properties in Shōwa 44 (1969).

=== Features ===
; Imperial Envoy Bridge  
: Spanning Miyagawa River within the shrine grounds.  
; Worship Hall  
: Single-story structure with a tiled roof and ''karahafu'' gables.  
; Middle Hall  
: Similar to the Worship Hall in design.  
; Main Hall  
: Nagare-zukuri style, with a copper roof.  
; Shigure Shrine  
: Enshrines {{ill|Miketsu-no-Kami|ja|水分神}}, {{ill|Raijin|en|Raijin|qid=Q12808082|lt=Raijin}}, {{ill|Kuraokami|ja|高龗神|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 淤加美神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q644201}}, and {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|海童神|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135505729}}. Known for hosting rainmaking rituals for the 24 villages of Iyo District.
